quotes: In July 2026, ciprocopan achieved its first global approval (in China), for the treatment of patients with PNH previously untreated with complement inhibitors.

A second marketing application for ciprocopan in China is currently under review, for the treatment of PNH patients previously treated with anti C5 therapy, with approval expected in 1Q27; additional ongoing clinical trials for ciprocopan in China include a Phase 3 in IgAN and a Phase 2 study in lupus nephritis.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the Q3 2026 Form 10-Q MD&A and November 4, 2026 Form 8-K earnings release.
competitive_position.claim: NXP100 targets a clinically validated Factor B pathway with a potential dosing convenience advantage from once-daily oral administration versus twice-daily oral iptacopan (Fabhalta), the only FDA-approved Factor B inhibitor, and injectable treatments.
quotes: Factor B is a key component of the complement system, a clinically validated target with an FDA approved CFBi approved in several chronic diseases including paroxysmal nocturnal hematoglobinuria (“PNH”), IgA Nephropathy (“IgAN”), and C3 glomerulonephritis (C3G).

NXP100’s PK/PD profile enables a once-daily administration compared to iptacopan, the only FDA-approved factor B inhibitor, which is administered orally twice-daily, providing a potential dosing convenience advantage which is an important attribute for diseases requiring life-long therapy.
Based on cross-trial comparisons, NXP100 demonstrated similar activity to iptacopan, with a similar safety profile.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the November 4, 2026 Form 8-K earnings release.
competitive_position.claim: In a head-to-head Phase 3 trial in China in complement-inhibitor-naive PNH patients, ciprocopan (NXP100) demonstrated a robust efficacy advantage over eculizumab (Soliris).
quotes: Phase 3 results from a study conducted in China of a head-to-head comparison of NXP100 versus eculizumab (Soliris) in patients with PNH naïve to complement inhibition was presented at the (European Hematology Association 2026 conference), demonstrating a robust efficacy advantage of ciprocopan versus Soliris.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the Q3 2026 Form 10-Q MD&A and November 4, 2026 Form 8-K earnings release.
competitive_position.claim: NXP200 is positioned as an oral, brain-penetrant paradox-breaker BRAF inhibitor intended to overcome first-generation BRAF-inhibitor resistance with reduced toxicity, and received China Breakthrough Therapy Designation in September 2026 for BRAF V600-mutant high-grade glioma.
quotes: The paradox breaking properties of NXP200 have the potential to address key unmet needs associated with BRAF inhibition, including emerging resistance to first generation BRAFi while reducing toxicities associated with their usage.

In September, NXP200 was granted Breakthrough Therapy Designation for the treatment of patients with BRAF V600-mutant, recurrent or progressive high-grade glioma by China’s Center for Drug Evaluation (CDE).

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the Q3 2026 Form 10-Q MD&A and November 4, 2026 Form 8-K earnings release.
competitive_position.claim: In ESMO 2026 Phase 1b data across 27 efficacy-evaluable BRAF V600 glioma patients, NXP200 monotherapy achieved an overall response rate of 40.0% in high-grade glioma and 42.9% in low-grade glioma, an 85.2% disease control rate, and responses in BRAF-inhibitor-pretreated patients.
quotes: As of the May 4, 2026 cutoff, 27 efficacy-evaluable patients with recurrent or progressive BRAF V600 glioma were treated with NXP200 monotherapy, including 20 patients with high-grade glioma and 7 with low-grade glioma.

Treatment with NXP200 resulted in an ORR of 40.0% in the high-grade glioma cohort, including 3 CRs (two confirmed and one preliminary) and 42.9% in the low-grade glioma cohort, including one confirmed CR.
81.5% of patients achieved tumor reduction and the Disease Control Rate (ORR plus SD) was 85.2%.
Notably, among the three patients previously treated with a BRAF inhibitor, two achieved a partial response and one had stable disease.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the FY2025 Form 10-K Item 1 Business.
competitive_position.claim: NXP900 targets a competitive whitespace where no kinase inhibitor is approved for SRC-active solid tumors and no selective YES1 inhibitor is FDA-approved, blocking both catalytic and scaffolding SRC functions by locking the kinase in its inactive conformation.
quotes: To date, no kinase inhibitor has been approved for the treatment of SRC-active solid tumor malignancies.
There are no FDA-approved selective YES1 inhibitors.

Unlike the approved and clinical-stage kinase inhibitors that inhibit only the catalytic (enzymatic) activity of SRC, NXP900 induces and locks SRC in its native inactive conformation, therefore inhibiting both the catalytic and scaffolding functions of the kinase, thus preventing phosphorylation and complex formation with its primary partners.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the FY2025 Form 10-K Item 1 Business, Q3 2026 Form 10-Q MD&A, and November 4, 2026 Form 8-K earnings release.
competitive_position.claim: NXP900 Phase 1a data showed no dose-limiting toxicity across evaluated doses and approximately 90% SRC phosphorylation inhibition at higher doses, supporting ongoing Phase 1b combination studies with osimertinib and lorlatinib.
quotes: In this Phase 1a portion of the study, a dose range of 20 to 300 mg/day was evaluated, and the dose-limiting toxicity level was not reached in that dose range.

Systemic exposure to NXP900 increased with higher doses, and a robust pharmacodynamic response of approximately 90% inhibition of SRC kinase phosphorylation was elicited at doses of 150 mg/day and higher, suggesting a potentially wide therapeutic window.

Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC): the clinical trials evaluating the combination of NXP900 plus osimertinib (Tagrisso™) in patients with NSCLC EGFR+ and the combination with lorlatinib (Lorbrena®) in patients with NSCLC ALK+ are ongoing.

growth_thesis.claim: NXP900 targets SRC and YES1 resistance pathways by locking the kinases in an inactive conformation and is advancing in ongoing Phase 1b combination trials with osimertinib and lorlatinib in non-small cell lung cancer plus a planned pancreatic cancer trial.
quotes: Unlike the approved and clinical-stage kinase inhibitors that inhibit only the catalytic (enzymatic) activity of SRC, NXP900 induces and locks SRC in its native inactive conformation, therefore inhibiting both the catalytic and scaffolding functions of the kinase, thus preventing phosphorylation and complex formation with its primary partners.

Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC): the clinical trials evaluating the combination of NXP900 plus osimertinib (Tagrisso™) in patients with NSCLC EGFR+ and the combination with lorlatinib (Lorbrena®) in patients with NSCLC ALK+ are ongoing.
An investigator-sponsored trial to evaluate the combination of NXP900 plus the recently approved daraxonrasib in patients with pancreatic cancer is planned at two leading medical centers in the U.S.

growth_thesis.basis: stated in P2 and P7, and inferred from NXP800 discontinuation in P3
growth_thesis.claim: For NXP900 to progress beyond Phase 1b, the combination regimens must demonstrate acceptable tolerability, absence of limiting drug-drug interactions, and clinical efficacy in NSCLC and planned studies.
quotes: issues related to combination regimens, including tolerability concerns, drug-drug interactions, or lack of efficacy;
During July 2025, we provided the final clinical data update for NXP800 and decided to cease development activities at this time.
Update from Phase 1b expected during the first half of 2027.

growth_thesis.basis: stated in P7 and P8, and corroborated in F1 and F3
growth_thesis.claim: Nuvectis expanded its cash and cash equivalents to $140.7 million as of September 30, 2026 via $115.0 million in follow-on offering gross proceeds and $39.5 million via its ATM, extending its expected cash runway into the second half of 2029 alongside a new $200 million shelf registration.
quotes: Cash and cash equivalents were $140.7 million as of September 30, 2026, compared to $31.6 million as of December 31, 2025.

In July, the Company raised $115.0 million in gross proceeds in a follow-on offering and additional $39.5 million of cash was raised via the existing ATM of which $37.0 million placed with a single healthcare dedicated fund.
We expect this funding to support our operations into the second half of 2029, providing a runway that extends well beyond multiple potential value-creating clinical and regulatory milestones.

On August 21, 2026, the Company expects to file a prospectus supplement (the “Prospectus Supplement”), relating to the Sale Agreement with the Securities and Exchange Commission (the “SEC”) under a new shelf Registration Statement on Form S-3 registering $200 million in securities, filed by the Company on August 21, 2026 (the “Registration Statement”).

growth_thesis.basis: stated in P1, P2, P5, and P6
growth_thesis.claim: To sustain development through late-stage trials and potential commercialization without generating product revenue, Nuvectis must manage rising R&D costs or raise additional dilutive or partnered capital, scale cGMP third-party manufacturing, and maintain patent protection.
quotes: We anticipate that our research and development expenses will increase substantially in connection with our ongoing and planned preclinical and clinical development activities in the near term and beyond.
Raising additional capital may cause dilution to our existing stockholders, or require us to relinquish proprietary rights.

We have not yet demonstrated our ability to successfully conduct or complete any clinical development program for our drug candidates, obtain marketing approvals, manufacture a commercial-scale product or arrange for a third party to do so on our behalf, or conduct sales, marketing and distribution activities necessary for successful product commercialization.
The statutory expiration for patents in this patent family is April 2036, without taking into account any possible patent term extension, where applicable.

growth_thesis.claim: Management intends to further expand the pipeline through business development and ex-U.S. collaborations and hired Dr. Dustin Little as SVP, Head of the Complement program to lead NXP100 regulatory and clinical execution.
quotes: deploying our differentiated and proven business development expertise to further expand our product candidate pipeline for patients with unmet medical needs; and
Dustin Little, MD, joined Nuvectis as Senior Vice President, Head of the Complement program, in September 2026.

material_events.claim: Nuvectis licensed exclusive world-wide development, manufacturing and commercial rights excluding China to NXP100 (ciprocopan) and NXP200 from Haisco Pharmaceutical Group, incurring a $20.0 million upfront payment.
quotes: In June 2026, we licensed exclusive world-wide development, manufacturing and commercial rights, excluding China, to NXP100/HSK39297/ciprocopan (“NXP100”) an oral, once daily, potent and selective small-molecule complement Factor B inhibitor (“CFBi”) in advanced stages of development.

In June 2026, we licensed exclusive world-wide development, manufacturing and commercial rights, excluding China, to NXP200/HSK42360 an inhibitor of the BRAF serine/threonine kinase (“BRAFi”) that has the potential to be a best-in-class, brain-penetrant paradox breaker, overcoming broad-spectrum BRAF-related drug resistance and to become a treatment option for multiple solid tumor types and primary brain cancer.
Completed in licensing of two potentially best-in-class drug candidates from Haisco Pharmaceutical Group and follow-on public offering anchored by leading healthcare investors.

The increase was primarily driven by the $20.0 million upfront payment for the NXP100 and NXP200 license agreement, $1.8 million in milestones associated with NXP900, a $1.2 million increase in employee compensation and benefits, $0.5 million increase in clinical trial expenses and a $0.1 million increase in manufacturing costs, partially offset by $2.0 million in license fees paid in 2025.

material_events.claim: Ciprocopan (NXP100) received marketing approval in China from the National Medical Products Administration for patients with PNH previously untreated with complement inhibitors.
quotes: In July 2026, ciprocopan achieved its first global approval (in China), for the treatment of patients with PNH previously untreated with complement inhibitors.
Ciprocopan (NXP100) has received marketing approval by the National Medical Products Administration (NMPA) in China for PNH patients previously untreated with complement inhibitors (treatment naive).

material_events.claim: A second marketing application for ciprocopan in China for PNH patients previously treated with anti C5 therapy is under review.
quotes: A second marketing application for ciprocopan in China is currently under review, for the treatment of PNH patients previously treated with anti C5 therapy, with approval expected in 1Q27; additional ongoing clinical trials for ciprocopan in China include a Phase 3 in IgAN and a Phase 2 study in lupus nephritis.

material_events.claim: Phase 3 head-to-head results comparing NXP100 versus eculizumab (Soliris) in complement-naive PNH patients were presented at the European Hematology Association conference.
quotes: Phase 3 results from a study conducted in China of a head-to-head comparison of NXP100 versus eculizumab (Soliris) in patients with PNH naïve to complement inhibition was presented at the (European Hematology Association 2026 conference), demonstrating a robust efficacy advantage of ciprocopan versus Soliris.

material_events.claim: Expanded NXP200 Phase 1b monotherapy data in recurrent or progressive BRAF V600-mutated gliomas were presented at the ESMO Congress, showing an ORR of 40.0% in high-grade glioma and 42.9% in low-grade glioma.
quotes: In October, expanded NXP200 Phase 1b data in patients with recurrent or progressive BRAF V600-mutated gliomas were presented at the 2026 ESMO Congress by our partner Haisco.

Treatment with NXP200 resulted in an ORR of 40.0% in the high-grade glioma cohort, including 3 CRs (two confirmed and one preliminary) and 42.9% in the low-grade glioma cohort, including one confirmed CR.

material_events.claim: Nuvectis commenced its Phase 1b combination clinical trial of NXP900 with osimertinib after initiating its Phase 1b single-agent study in August 2025 and completing its Phase 1a and DDI studies in July 2025.

In July 2025, we announced the completion of the Phase 1a part of the clinical trial in which we evaluated the safety, tolerability and pharmacokinetic properties of NXP900 in patients with advanced solid tumors to identify potential doses and dosing schedules for the Phase 1b.

In July 2025, in advance of exploring combinations of NXP900 with EGFR and ALK inhibitors, we announced the completion and topline results from our clinical drug-drug interaction (“DDI”) study in healthy volunteers.
In August 2025, we announced the initiation of the Phase 1b expansion portion of the study.

risks.basis: Stated in P2, P3, P5, P7, and P1
risks.claim: Clinical development of NXP100, NXP200, and NXP900 carries high risk of trial failure, toxicity, or insufficient efficacy, as demonstrated when Nuvectis ceased clinical development of NXP800 after its Phase 1b study.
quotes: Clinical drug development involves a lengthy and expensive process with uncertain outcomes, clinical trials are difficult to design and implement, and any of our clinical trials could produce unsuccessful results or fail at any stage in the process.
Following the completion of the NXP800 Phase 1b study, we decided to cease the clinical development of NXP800 as we assess possible next steps, if any, in the development of the compound.

Additionally, any positive results of preclinical studies and early clinical data of a drug candidate may not be predictive of the final results of the early clinical trial or of later-stage clinical trials.

risks.basis: Stated in P2, P6, and P7; uncertainty over U.S. acceptance of China data is inferred from the ongoing FDA discussions in P7 and regulatory risk disclosures in P2
risks.claim: Regulatory approvals in the U.S. and other jurisdictions are uncertain and could be delayed or denied if the FDA rejects China clinical data for ciprocopan, requires additional trials or companion diagnostics, or experiences agency funding disruptions.
quotes: Communications with the U.S. FDA about the potential of the clinical data package that led to the approval of ciprocopan in China for the treatment of PNH to support a marketing application for NXP100 in the U.S. are well underway and an update is expected by year-end; Nuvectis continues to explore additional opportunities and an IND submission, for an indication beyond PNH, is expected by year-end.

If a companion diagnostic is essential to the safe and effective use of any of our current and future product candidates, the FDA may require that the companion diagnostic meets the applicable standard for safety and effectiveness or for substantial equivalence for use with our product candidates before either the product candidates or companion diagnostic may be marketed in the United States.
Disruptions at the FDA and other agencies may also slow the time necessary for new product candidates to be reviewed and/or approved by necessary government agencies.

risks.basis: Stated in P1, P3, P5, and P7; completion of the $3.0 million cumulative UoE fundraising cap is inferred from $1.2 million paid through December 31, 2025 in P3 plus $1.8 million in Q3 2026 in P5
risks.claim: Nuvectis relies on in-licensed rights for its pipeline and faces license termination risk if it breaches diligence or payment obligations, including up to $45.5 million in pre-approval milestones and up to $279.5 million in regulatory and sales milestones under the University of Edinburgh license.
quotes: UoE may terminate the License Agreement if we: (i) cease to carry on the business regarding the treatment, prevention and/or diagnosis of human diseases; (ii) discontinue the development of the licensed products which are the subject of the License Agreement; (iii) dispose of our assets or business in whole or in material part; (iv) challenge the validity, ownership, or enforceability of the exclusively licensed technology; (v) contest the secret or substantial nature of certain know-how subject to the License Agreement; or (vi) breach certain diligence obligations or fail to pay any amount due under the License Agreement within a specified time frame.

As of December 31, 2025, we were obligated to make up to $45.5 million in milestone payments to the UoE related to pre-approval milestones, up to $279.5 million in regulatory and commercial sales milestones, mid-single digit to 8% royalties on a tiered basis based on net sales and 2.5% of the gross amount of each of our fund raisings up to a cumulative total of $3.0 million, of which $1.2 million has already been paid through December 31, 2025.

The increase in research and development expense during the three months ended September 30, 2026, was primarily driven by a $19.8 million increase in license fees due to $20.0 million related to our license agreement with Haisco Inc, $1.8 million in license fees to the University of Edinburgh related to our fund raising milestones, partially offset by $2.0 million in milestone achievements in 2025, $1.2 million increase in employee compensation and benefits, and $0.6 million increase in clinical trial and manufacturing expenses related to the development of NXP100, NXP200 and NXP900.

risks.claim: Nuvectis depends on third-party CROs, CMOs, and clinical trial sites over whose regulatory compliance, schedules, and performance it has limited control.
quotes: We rely, and plan to continue to rely, on CROs, contract manufacturing organizations (“CMOs”) and clinical trial sites to ensure the proper and timely conduct of our clinical trials.
Although we have and expect that we will have agreements in place with CROs and CMOs governing their contracted activities and conduct, we will have limited influence over their actual performance.

risks.claim: Nuvectis cannot guarantee enforceable patent protection for its product candidates, as patents may be challenged or narrowed and lengthy development could leave little remaining patent term after approval.
quotes: The statutory expiration for patents in this patent family is April 2036, without taking into account any possible patent term extension, where applicable.
As a result, we cannot guarantee that any of our current or future product candidates will be protected or remain protectable by enforceable patents.

In addition, because of the extensive time required for clinical development and regulatory review of any current or future product candidates we may develop, it is possible that, before any current or future product candidates can be commercialized, any related patent may expire or remain in force for only a short period following commercialization, thereby limiting the protection such patent would afford the respective product and any competitive advantage such patent may provide.

risks.basis: Stated in P6, P1, and P7
risks.claim: Nuvectis has never completed a clinical development program, manufactured commercial-scale product, or conducted sales and marketing, and may fail to transition from an R&D organization to a commercial company.
quotes: While all our product candidates are in the clinical development phase, we have not yet demonstrated our ability to successfully conduct or complete any clinical development program for any of our drug candidates, obtain marketing approvals, manufacture a commercial-scale product or arrange for a third party to do so on our behalf, or conduct sales, marketing and distribution activities necessary for successful product commercialization.
We may need to transition at some point in time from a company with a research and development focus to a company capable of supporting commercial activities related to the full product life cycle.
We may not be successful in such a transition.

risks.claim: U.S. or foreign tariffs, trade restrictions, and retaliatory trade measures could inflate raw material, reagent, and equipment costs and disrupt supply chains and logistics.
